issue.title: Full check of the 11/5 manuscript
issue.body:
Hi Elliot,

I went over the 11/5 manuscript with my Claude research system, and below are the main points it found (none of them should affect the results).

To give you an idea of what was done, every proof in the paper was read in full, with the hardest ones read a second time and their steps rederived, the cited sources were checked where they were used (statements and hypotheses, not re-proved), the computations were redone, and the precision polynomial was rebuilt from the archive. 

**1. Mazur 1992, and his Conjecture 2.** l. 84 and Cor. 13.1. Both the conjecture and the remark that it would rule out a Diophantine definition of Z in Q go back to B. Mazur, *The topology of rational points*, Experiment. Math. 1 (1992), 35–45. Conjectures 1–3 are stated there (pp. 35–36) with the same numbers as in the 1995 update the paper cites, and on pp. 36–37 Mazur notes that Conjecture 3 would imply that Z is not Diophantine in Q, by the same projection argument as the proof of Cor. 13.1; the 1995 update repeats the remark (p. 166). Mazur derives Conjecture 3 from Conjecture 2 (1992, p. 36), so Theorem 1.1 refutes Conjecture 2 as well. *Suggested fix:* cite Mazur 1992 and the 1995 remark at l. 84 and in Cor. 13.1, and credit the argument to Mazur.

**2. Prop 8.9: which coordinate.** Prop 8.9, l. 3987–4141, with (4.6) at l. 4045; used in Prop 9.6 (l. 4912, 4920), at l. 5201, and in the final contradiction (l. 5652, 5729). The statement gives a formula for v₂u_prim(0), where u_prim is the generic coordinate of Def 8.7 (l. 3877–3892). The proof, however, computes only the coordinate of the central tensor z₀⊗λ₀ (l. 4061–4080). The statement's phrase "with the central class and functional of Lemma 8.8" (l. 3992–3993) does not say which of the two is meant. Prop 9.6 and the final contradiction need the specialised generic coordinate. The facts that make the two equal are in the paper, but later and uncited: (a) generic cohomology (1,1) at a known simple zero (l. 4928–4934); (b) the base-change argument at equal generic and central dimensions (no t-disks), written out only for the base in Lemma 8.11 (l. 4353–4368), which applies verbatim; it also gives regularity at (t), shown in general at l. 4976–5194. None of these uses (4.6), so there is no circularity. (OpenAI's 2-converse preprint, item 7, states (b) as Lemma 5.8.) *Suggested fix:* before Prop 8.9, state l. 4353–4368 as a lemma for any constituent whose generic and central rational dimensions agree; cite or move l. 4928–4934; say in the statement that u_prim(0) is the specialised generic coordinate; and add a paragraph to the proof invoking these with l. 3982–3985.

**3. What's new in Cor. 13.3.** Cor. 13.3 implies that HTP(Q) has Turing degree 0′, which is Corollary 7.1 of OpenAI's "Hilbert's tenth problem over the rational numbers" (6 Oct 2026; "the H10 preprint" below), p. 56; that paper notes (p. 57) that its argument "does not establish many-one completeness of H10(Q)". *Suggested fix:* cite it here, and say that the new part is 0′ ≤_m HTP(Q), obtained from Theorem 1.1 through Cor. 13.2; HTP(Q) ≤_m 0′ is standard.

**4. Kato's Thm 13.4 at p = 2.** l. 1884–1892, l. 6788–6790 (App. D) and App. E par. 7 (l. 7206–7241). Kato proves 13.4 "By [Pe4, Ru4, KK4]" (*Astérisque* 295, p. 226). Perrin-Riou [Pe4] (AIF 48, 1998) assumes p odd (§1.1.1, p. 1234). So at p = 2 the theorem rests on Kato, *Kodai Math. J.* 22 (1999) [KK4], and Rubin, *Euler systems* [Ru4]. Each needs one hypothesis beyond 13.4 as printed:

- Kato 1999, 0.6(ii) (p. 317), asks for σ in Gal(Q̄/Q^ab), not just in Gal(Q̄/Q(μ_{2^∞})).

- Rubin's Hyp(K_∞, V)(ii) asks for V to be irreducible over G_{Q_∞}. At p = 2 this does not follow from 13.4(iv)+(v) in general, since Q(√2) ⊂ Q_∞.

For T⊗χ both hold, by the open-image fact the paper already uses. Kato 1999 allows p = 2 (Thm 0.8, p. 318). In the 1999 Arizona Winter School draft of Rubin's book, Thms II.3.2 and II.3.4 carry no p > 2 hypothesis, and §V.3 says "We now allow p = 2". *Suggested fix:* for p = 2, cite Kato 1999 Thm 0.8 (p. 318) and/or Rubin's Iwasawa-theoretic divisibility (Thm II.3.4 of the 1999 draft). Add one line: the unipotent can be taken in G_{Q^ab}, and V⊗χ is irreducible over G_{Q(μ_{2^∞})}.

**5. The saved polynomial against the text.** l. 135–137 and l. 6262–6266, with App. C. The proof of Theorem 1.1 credits statement B (l. 105–107) to §§2 and 12 and App. C. The end of §11 (l. 6263–6265) says that the literal substitutions of §2 and App. C identify the polynomial of Val with the saved root P_\*. But §2 and App. C give only decoding rules, and §12 bounds sizes. Nothing printed says which saved template encodes which relation of the text: that `value.test` is Test of §11, `value.close_coordinates` is Close, `value.exceptions` is the exceptional branch, `test_group` is the twelve tests of §6, `pole` is Q_pole of §5, and the composition recipes give Val. So a reader can't check the identification from the page. Spot checks of the decoded templates agree: `pole` is Q_pole squared, and the top-level constraints of `value.test` and `test_group` are the tests of §11 and §6 (for `test_group`, with the σ below). One place is less explicit than the template: at l. 1172–1173 (§6, p. 17) the text lists "three differences of the corresponding L-ratios" without saying that the primed ratio is conjugated, while `test_group` takes tests 9–11 to be A_i − σ(A′_i), with A_i = L(z(U_i))/L(z(H)) and A′_i = L(z(V_i))/L(z(V_0)). The template is right: the argument at l. 1194–1213 needs the σ, since tests 5–8 put V_0 and V_i in the formal group at the conjugate place σv, and §11 prints it in the parallel tests (l. 6137–6138). *Suggested fix:* a table mapping each template and composition recipe to its displayed relation and constraint list, or a pointer to a checker that does this. At l. 1172–1173, write "three differences A_i − σ(A′_i)", defining A′_i as above.

**6. The valuation step in §6.** §6, l. 1196–1198 (p. 18): "The trace and Lemma 5.1 force one common group and place where the first eight tests have valuation at least one and the last four at least 25." The conclusion is right, but the step is not written, and the quick reading (some group has every factor 1 + RC_{gj}² a unit) fails once v_p(R_0) ≥ 3. Write δ = v_p(R_0). At a positive odd contact prime outside S_mul this is v_p(t − c) for the contact c with t ≡ c, so it is odd and positive. Write α = v_p(R) = δ + 2v_p(a) (l. 1179–1180). Then α is odd and α ≤ δ, since v_p(a) ≤ 0. These are the δ and α of Lemma 11.1 (l. 6157–6161). Example: δ = α = 3, and in every group one factor has valuation −1 and the rest are units. Then v_p(Θ) can be 1, and the pole input R/Θ² has valuation 1, which Lemma 5.1 allows, though no group has all factors units. An argument that works: a test below its threshold at a place makes its factor's valuation at most α − 2δ, so v(W_g^{-1}) ≥ 2δ − α there. If this happens for every group at every place above p, then v_p(Θ) ≥ 2δ − α and v_p(R/Θ²) ≤ 3α − 4δ ≤ −δ < 0, which is odd, contradicting Lemma 5.1. *Suggested fix:* add the two inequalities α ≤ δ and v_p(Θ) ≥ 2δ − α.

**7. Credit to OpenAI's two preprints.** Thm 5.3 (l. 1005–1011) is the case E = E_ℓ, s₂(E) = 1 of Thm 1.1 of OpenAI's "A pointwise 2-converse for elliptic curves with rational two-torsion" (7 Oct 2026). It is also the case c₂(E) = 1 of Thm 1.1 of OpenAI's "Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves" (7 Oct 2026). §§7–9 and App. E–G prove RC along the 2-converse preprint's route. Four of App. B's sources are sections of it at openai/math commit 4eaee875: S30 is its §2, S18 its §4, S29 its §5 and S32 its §9 (l. 6633–6647). The paper proves this case itself, so the citation is only for credit, but the preprint isn't in the bibliography yet, and App. B gives those four sections only as file names. Similarly, §§3–6 adapt the H10 preprint closely (§3 follows the proof of its Prop. 2.1, Thm 4.1 the method of its §4, §5 its §3, and Prop. 6.2 its Lemma 6.1), and it is cited only at l. 53–54. *Suggested fix:* cite the 2-converse Thm 1.1 at Thm 5.3 and at the opening of §7 (l. 1760–1796), and say that RC is its case E = E_ℓ. Name the preprint and commit in App. B. For the H10 preprint, a local reference at each adapted step would do; I can send a step-by-step map.

**8. History of the problem.** A short history after l. 54 would help readers: J. Robinson, *Definability and decision problems in arithmetic*, J. Symbolic Logic 14 (1949), 98–114, for the first first-order definition of Z in Q; B. Poonen, *Characterizing integers among rational numbers with a universal-existential formula*, Amer. J. Math. 131 (2009), 675–682, for a ∀∃-definition; and J. Koenigsmann, *Defining Z in Q*, Ann. of Math. 183 (2016), 73–93, for a universal definition (Theorem 1), so that Q∖Z is Diophantine (Corollary 2).

**9. Lemma 7.16 at primes off the filter.** Lemma 7.16 (l. 2628–2654). The prime p chosen at l. 2643–2644 (p ≡ 1 mod 4, (ℓ/p) = −1) can never lie in the square filter: by reciprocity it is a nonsquare modulo some prime of ℓ, and those primes divide N. So the lemma needs the no-seed congruence a_p ≡ p + 1 (mod 8) at good K-split primes off the filter. App. G derives it there (l. 10351–10353, 10448–10450). The lemma says only "at the required good K-split primes" (l. 2638). *Suggested fix:* "at every fresh good K-split prime outside the support, in or out of the filter".

The rest of the things found are nitpicks so I can send those too if you want to see those as well.

comments.body:
Thank you for the detailed review. All nine points are addressed in **Version 10**, with the polynomial specifications, coefficient files and numerical bounds unchanged. The [TeX](https://github.com/elliotglazer/diophantine-z-q/blob/8b1db08764b4935c37676ffa36f58ae084fa2ff0/manuscripts/quartic_v10.tex), [PDF](https://github.com/elliotglazer/diophantine-z-q/blob/8b1db08764b4935c37676ffa36f58ae084fa2ff0/manuscripts/quartic_v10.pdf), and [detailed dispositions and source checks](https://github.com/elliotglazer/diophantine-z-q/blob/8b1db08764b4935c37676ffa36f58ae084fa2ff0/docs/manuscript-revisions/version10/README.md) are available.

1. **Mazur.** Added the 1992 reference, credited the projection observation, and included the consequence for Conjecture 2. The source record distinguishes checking the 1992 publication metadata from reading the conjectures and observation in the 1995 update; the original 1992 scan was not obtained.
2. **Determinant coordinate.** Added the general specialization lemma before the calibration, established the required generic dimensions without using the calibration, and identified the coordinate as the specialized generic coordinate. The application uses the actual regular class and functional, not dimension equality alone.
3. **Computability attribution.** Credited OpenAI's Corollary 7.1 for Turing completeness and isolated the additional many-one direction obtained from the integer definition. The reverse many-one reduction is the standard rational-point enumeration.
4. **Kato at two.** Made the direct application of the published 1999 Theorem 0.8 explicit, including the unipotent in the abelian kernel and irreducibility over the cyclotomic extension. The expanded argument also compares the 1999 full-cohomology convention with the 2004 j-star convention and tracks the actual retained class and its coordinate ideal. It does not rely on the odd-prime Perrin-Riou theorem or an unpublished Rubin draft.
5. **Saved polynomial.** Printed the conjugated primed ratios and added the template/recipe dictionary, including the saved pole square, guards, shared shift and witness scope. The saved polynomial itself did not need changing.
6. **Valuations.** Printed the inequalities involving delta and alpha and the trace contradiction. The proof does not assert that some group has only unit factors. Your counterexample correctly rules out that shortcut.
7. **OpenAI credit.** Added both converse preprints, the explicit specialization at RC, local attribution at the adapted steps, and the source-section mapping at the pinned commit. These references give attribution; the revision does not add an assumption of a new unpublished theorem.
8. **History.** Added Robinson, Poonen and Koenigsmann with their respective definability results.
9. **Off-filter primes.** Stated explicitly that the congruence covers every fresh good K-split prime outside the support, including primes outside the coefficient filter, and explained why the chosen prime is outside it.

We also checked the earlier research record to distinguish missing printed explanations from previously absent mathematics. That [historical comparison, with excerpts and hashes](https://github.com/elliotglazer/diophantine-z-q/blob/8b1db08764b4935c37676ffa36f58ae084fa2ff0/docs/audit-history/issue2/README.md) found prior justifications for the determinant specialization, template semantics and off-filter scope. In particular, the complete maximum-valuation proof for point 6 was already in the November 3 source and was pinned in an earlier audit. It never used the all-unit shortcut. For Kato, an earlier applicability audit explicitly recorded the stronger abelian-kernel condition; Version 10 gives the direct route and convention comparison a fuller connected treatment.

Those earlier notes do not excuse omissions in the manuscript. The review correctly identified where a reader could not recover the argument from the printed application. Describing all these changes as newly filled mathematical gaps would also misstate the history.

To reduce recurrence, the repository now has an [audit integration protocol](https://github.com/elliotglazer/diophantine-z-q/blob/8b1db08764b4935c37676ffa36f58ae084fa2ff0/docs/audit-history/PROTOCOL.md) and a register separating historical justification from manuscript incorporation. Each item points to evidence and an exact consuming passage. CI checks those bindings and rejects stale evidence, missing dispositions, pending incorporation, or a new manuscript selection without an updated binding. These are structural checks, not a machine verification of the mathematics or a claim of independent validation of the whole manuscript.

The issue remains open for your recheck. Please send the remaining smaller comments as well.

I rechecked v10 against the nine points (not the new §§14–18 or Apps. I–J). All nine are addressed, and the new arguments in 2, 4 and 6 are right, except for one missing step in point 4's new Kato 1999 route.

**Point 4.** At l. 12680–12690, Kato 1999, Thm 0.8 is applied to the classes (K8). Kato's Euler system needs classes at every level divisible by his N, which v10 takes to be N_K = 2Nd (l. 12682–12683), but (K8) is only defined when prime(m) ∩ Σ = {2} (l. 12398), Kato 2004's index set Ξ. Since Σ contains 3 and the primes of d, none of those levels is covered, and Kato's ξ is never identified with y_{2^∞}. The fix is short and changes nothing else. Replacement for l. 12680–12684 (through "need not be inverted."):

> Put N_K = 2Nd and N′ = c d_s; these are coprime by (K5), since d | F. For every m with N_K | m and (m, N′) = 1, define y_m by the formula (K8). Proposition 8.12 applies with S_{Dml} = S_{Dm} when l | m, and with S_{Dml} − S_{Dm} = {l} when l ∤ m. With the corestriction identity before (K9), this gives (0.1.1) of [kato1999] with P_l(l^{−1}σ_l^{−1}) = E_l(χ) of (K9). Since S_{D N_K 2^n} = S_{D 2^n} = prime(2Nd), the norm of y_{N_K 2^n} to Q(ζ_{2^n}) is y_{2^n}. Hence the element ξ of [kato1999, 0.7], with d = 1 there, is the image of y_{2^∞}.

**Point 1.** The 1992 paper is free on Project Euclid: https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.em/1048709114. Conjecture 1 is on p. 35, Conjectures 2 and 3 are on p. 36, and the projection argument is on pp. 36–37.

Thank you. You are right: the Version 10 paragraph did not establish the index-set extension required by Kato 1999 or identify its supplied class. Our earlier review checked several hypotheses but missed this connecting argument.

[Version 11 TeX](https://github.com/elliotglazer/diophantine-z-q/blob/650b298a2a18fa956f8859f3ca80e9d7c8cedd82/manuscripts/quartic_v11.tex) and [PDF](https://github.com/elliotglazer/diophantine-z-q/blob/650b298a2a18fa956f8859f3ca80e9d7c8cedd82/manuscripts/quartic_v11.pdf) now define K8 for every positive m coprime to c d_s. With N_K=2Nd and N'_K=c d_s, this covers every index in 1999 Section 0.1. The added passage near K8 and on page 170 verifies both norm cases using 2004 Proposition 8.12, then displays the exact corestriction identity from N_K 2^n to 2^n. Equal construction supports remove the Euler factors; transitivity gives no field-degree multiplier. It distinguishes the varying construction support from the fixed inverted support and identifies the Section 0.7 class with the retained dyadic class. The optional fixed lattice factor is explicit and is a unit at the away-from-two localizations used here.

The repair was checked against the original source pages, then independently reviewed in the exact final TeX. The [review records and precise scope](https://github.com/elliotglazer/diophantine-z-q/blob/650b298a2a18fa956f8859f3ca80e9d7c8cedd82/docs/manuscript-revisions/version11/README.md) include the final reviewer-authored acceptance. Polynomial tables, bounds and the abstract are unchanged. This is acceptance of this repair, not a fresh whole-manuscript audit.

The original Mazur 1992 PDF was also obtained, and pages 35–37 were read directly. They confirm the variety convention, Conjectures 2 and 3, and the projection observation. The dated source record preserves the earlier access limitation as history rather than rewriting it.

We have strengthened the [review protocol](https://github.com/elliotglazer/diophantine-z-q/blob/650b298a2a18fa956f8859f3ca80e9d7c8cedd82/docs/audit-history/PROTOCOL.md) and executable checks. Every changed application must compare required and constructed domains, transition maps, the exact resulting object and its downstream consumer. Approval is bound to the exact edits, contract and manuscript. The follow-up ledger must include the latest finding in its pinned issue snapshot. Independent review found two weaknesses in the first implementation; both were fixed. The final checks reject 26 test mutations, including missing index coverage, missing class identification, stale approval and an omitted latest finding. These are record-integrity checks, not automated verification of the mathematics.

The [updated research supplement](https://github.com/elliotglazer/diophantine-z-q/blob/650b298a2a18fa956f8859f3ca80e9d7c8cedd82/research/version11/README.md) contains the repair, source audits, protocol and reproducible review checks.
